<!-- pr-reviewer: f35bd14e8367883fdcc815e607e6f590f451bce4 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The safety logic holds on every route I tried. The blockers are pinning gaps: two tolerances and several new refusals can be loosened or deleted and every test still passes. There is also one face case that silently does not seed.

### What looks good
- `SlotBound` is world-free and refuses by name with numbers. `confine` only refuses. It never clips or shrinks a typed slot, so nothing is cut silently in a smaller form.
- Seeding happens inside `SetOperationGeometry` / `CreateOperation`. `prev` holds the whole `Operation`, so one undo restores both the source and the typed a/b/width (pinned).
- The `DepthLaw::Section` route is real. The post filters `cache.warnings` by `blocks_post()` (`crates/app/src/posting.rs:1066`), so a picked slot convicted by the section or solid law holds the post.
- The 3+2 tilt with picks is still refused before any of this runs (`job.rs:214`). Picks and endpoints are both world XY, the same frame `selection.rs` uses for picked pockets, so a WCS offset moves both together.
- MCP parity comes through the same commands, and an MCP pin covers it. The decision file is present, `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched, no PNGs changed, there is no build.rs, dependency or `.github` change, and both new modules carry provenance lines.

### Local results (trial-merged with upstream/main @ incl. #1513, clean merge, macOS)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build `-p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --no-run` | ok |
| motion `--lib` (incl. 7 `slot_room` pins) | 299 passed, 5 ignored |
| motion `machining2d` / `trochoid_slot` | 66 / 10 passed |
| app `slot_picks` | 7 passed |
| app `slot_caps` / `trochoid_confine` / `trochoid_op` | 4 / 6 / 5 passed |
| app `operations` | 119 passed, 6 ignored |
| app `posting` / `mcp` / `mcp_order` / `commands_undo` | 17 / 22 / 3 / 30 passed |
| app `area_picks` / `area_open` / `circular_pick` / `pick_doors` / `pick_agnostic` | 5 / 10 / 4 / 6 / 5 passed |
| app `verify` / `golden_cl` / `solid_law` / `mill2d_b` / `mill2d_c` | 21 / 32 / 4 / 9 / 9 passed |
| app `units_in_refusals` / `tilt` / `project_roundtrip` / `scripting` / `--lib` | 5 / 8 / 73 / 18 / 194 passed |
| ui `--lib` (incl. `slot_pick_page_tests`) / `operations` / `boundary_picks` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 711 / 31 / 6 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Routes probed with local scratch tests (not pushed):**
- **Two top edges that bound material** (pocket rim y 8 and block edge y 25): this seeds a 17 mm slot in the solid wall. It generates with blocking `cuts past the finish surface` and `below the clearance plane inside stock`, so the post is held. Covered by the Section and solid law.
- **Channel narrower than the tool** (8 mm pocket, 10 mm tool): refused, `slot is narrower than the tool`.
- **One edge / three edges:** refused by name (`this selection has 1 open edge` / `3 open edges`).
- **Face pick, slot shifted 1 mm into the wall:** refused, `runs 1.000 mm outside the picked face`.
- **Round-ended (stadium) floor face, 30 x 16, tessellated at 8 chords per quarter (0.039 mm sag):** see request 3.

**Mutation check (each applied alone, then reverted; motion `slot_room` + app `slot_picks`):**
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `FIT_TOL` 0.01 -> 0.1 or 0.5 | **all pins pass** |
| `STRAIGHT_TOL` 0.01 -> 0.1 or 1.0 | **all pins pass** |
| `face_overshoot`: drop the "slot boundary outside the region" sampling (`if !region.contains(p)`) | **all pins pass** |
| `slot_bound_of`: `([e1, e2], 0)` -> `([e1, e2, ..], 0)` (3+ edges silently use the first two) | **all pins pass** |
| `slot_bound_of`: `([], 1)` -> `(_, 1)` (face + edges silently uses the face) | **all pins pass** |
| `slot_bound_of`: Patch/Vertex arm -> `continue` | **all pins pass** |
| `from_face`: drop "bounds no area" | **all pins pass** |
| `fit`: drop "no width" | **all pins pass** |
| `from_edges`: drop "first edge has no length" | **all pins pass** |
| `confine`: drop the finite / width > 0 guard | **all pins pass** |
| `CreateOperation`: drop the seed | **all pins pass** |
| `confine` across / along / out checks; island vertex check; `fit` too-short; fit's self-confine; edges no-overlap | caught |
| generate: drop `confine`; Slot out of `DepthLaw::Section`; preview `confine_slot`; `SetOperationGeometry` seed | caught (4 / 1 / 2 / 3 pins) |

The PR body says "M6: FIT_TOL loosened to 5 mm, 3 fail". That holds at 5 mm, but the pins never come within 0.5 mm of the limit, so a 50x loosening goes unnoticed.

### Requested before merge
1. **Near-miss pins for both tolerances** (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room.rs:18-23`). Add a slot that is 0.02 mm too wide, 0.02 mm too long and 0.02 mm past the picks, each refused, plus one 0.005 mm past that is accepted. Do this for both the edge room and the face room. Also add an edge that bows 0.02 mm (refused) and one that bows 0.005 mm (accepted). Then loosening either constant to 0.1 must turn a pin red.
2. **Pin each new refusal so that deleting its line turns a test red** (the standing rule for refusals):
   - The face law's outside-sampling (`slot_room.rs`, `face_overshoot`, the `if !region.contains(p)` loop). This is the only thing that refuses a slot placed past a picked face's side. No unit or app test reaches it: the floor-face shifts that would need it are absent. A 1 mm sideways shift on a picked face fails only through this loop (I checked it by hand).
   - `slot_bound_of`'s selection-shape refusals (`crates/app/src/operation/slot_pick.rs`): one edge, three edges, face plus edges, a vertex or patch pick, and a pick that has gone.
   - `from_face` no-area, `fit` no-width, `from_edges` zero-length first edge, and `confine`'s non-finite or non-positive width guard (unit pins are enough).
   - `CreateOperation` seeding on picks (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/create.rs:88-92`). The body claims it, but no test creates a Slot directly on a Selection. Add one, including that undo removes it.
3. **A tessellated round-ended slot face does not seed, and the reason is hidden.** Fixture: `block_with_pocket(25, 25, &rounded_rect(15, 8, 8, 8), 10, 20)`. With 8 chords per quarter the chord sag is 0.039 mm, so `fit()` fails its own confine (`runs 0.039 mm outside the picked face`). `slot_from_picks` swallows that at `tracing::debug!` (`slot_pick.rs:107-110`). The typed slot stays, and the user is told `52.000 mm long end to end, but the picked face is only 30.000 mm long`, not why the pick seeded nothing. With 16 or more chords per quarter it seeds (sag 0.0096 mm, just under `FIT_TOL`). STEP tessellation is often coarser than that, and this is the issue's own "a face gives the slot that fits that face" case. Either make `fit()` inscribe the slot, shrinking width and length by the measured overshoot so it confines (a smaller slot is the safe direction), or surface the fit refusal in the page echo and at generate when the picks did not seed. Pin it with the 8-chord stadium fixture above.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- With an Entity or whole-model source, a Slot still takes `DepthLaw::None`. `with_nothing_picked_the_typed_endpoints_rule_as_before` pins that a slot through the pocket wall raises no gouge. That behaviour predates this PR, but the issue's third bullet expects "the model gouge check still decides". A follow-up issue may be worth filing if a part-model source is meant to be kept rather than removed.
- `SetOperationGeometry` re-seeds a/b/width on every pick command, so re-picking the same edges overwrites a slot the user had shortened. That is reasonable by design, and worth one line in the decision file.
- `face_overshoot` checks only the region's vertices inside the slot. A region edge that crosses the slot without a vertex inside it, narrower than `SIDE_STEP` (0.5 mm), slips between the samples. The solid law at the post would still convict it. Measuring segment-to-segment distance from region edges to the slot's centre segment would make it exact.
- The second commit's subject `style(slot):` uses a type that is not in AGENTS.md's list (`refactor`/`chore` would fit). `generate.rs` (3434 lines) grows by 12 lines; flagged only.
- The UI recomputes `slot_fit_of` (bound + face sampling) every frame for a Slot draft. That is cheap at these sizes, but noted.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b1e25d274dc99440c3ea0dc5942c0953edbc37ca -->
**Needs changes before merge.** This is a delta review from f35bd14e to b1e25d27, with the merge of main left out. All three asks from the last review are met, and the inscribe is safe on every face I tried. One gap is left: the line that makes the new face law exact can be deleted and every pin still passes. A one-test fix closes it.

### What looks good
- **Tolerances are pinned from both sides.** Loosening `FIT_TOL` to 0.1 turns 4 pins red, and loosening `STRAIGHT_TOL` to 0.1 turns 1 red.
- **Every listed refusal now has a pin.** Each one turned a test red when I deleted it (table below).
- **The inscribe is safe.** I checked it independently, without the PR's own `face_overshoot`: I sampled 8000 points on the capsule outline and measured each region vertex's distance to the slot's centre segment. Every inscribed slot sits fully inside its face. The endpoints stay put and only the radius is drawn in, so the capsule shrinks evenly on every side. After that, `fit()` still runs the full `confine`, so even an inscribe that went wrong could never seed a slot outside the face.

  | Stadium 30 x 16, r 8, chords per quarter | sag | result | worst outside (independent check) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 16 | 0.0096 | seeded at 16.000 (inside `FIT_TOL`, no shrink) | 0.0096 |
  | 8 | 0.0385 | inscribed, width 15.923 | 0.000 |
  | 4 | 0.1537 | inscribed, width 15.693 | 0.000 |
  | 3 | 0.2726 | inscribed, width 15.455 | 0.000 |
  | 2 | 0.6090 | inscribed, width 14.782 | 0.000 |
  | 1 | 2.343 | refused by name (`room 21.213 mm long for a 21.213 mm wide slot`) | - |
  | r 20, 1 chord (120 x 40) | 5.858 | over the 2.0 mm cap: refused by name, `holds no straight slot ... runs 5.858 mm outside` | - |
- **The cap holds.** When the overshoot is over the cap, the loop breaks and `confine` refuses by name. Nothing is shrunk silently past the cap.
- **`judge` is used at all three doors** (generation, preview and page echo). It adds "the picks seed no slot: ..." only when `fit()` fails, and its pin catches a plain `confine` swapped in.
- **The face law is now exact.** The thin-wall case from the first review is now refused. My test: a 10 x 30 face with a 0.1 mm slit hole across the slot, with every slit vertex outside the slot's outline (slit x 10.5-19.5, slot x 12-18). Result: `runs 3.000 mm outside the picked face`. The wall law plus the end law decide containment exactly: a capsule that touches no boundary is wholly inside or wholly outside.
- **Housekeeping.** The new module `slot_room_face.rs` has a provenance line. All files are under 400 lines. The commit subjects are conventional, no PNGs, `CHANGELOG.md` or process files changed, and the merge of main took no hand resolution.

### Local results (b1e25d27 trial-merged with upstream/main 67329c86: clean, macOS, sccache)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build `-p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app` tests | ok |
| motion `--lib` (incl. `slot_room` tests + 8 new pins) | 307 passed, 5 ignored |
| app `slot_picks` / `slot_pick_refusals` | 7 / 3 passed |
| app `slot_caps` / `trochoid_confine` / `trochoid_op` | 4 / 6 / 5 passed |
| app `operations` | 119 passed, 6 ignored |
| app `posting` / `mcp` / `commands_undo` / `--lib` | 17 / 22 / 30 / 194 passed |
| ui `--lib` | not run: the delta changes no UI file (the UI files in the diff come from main) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Mutations.** I applied each one alone and reverted it, then ran motion `--lib slot_room` and app `slot_picks` + `slot_pick_refusals`.

| Mutation | Pins red |
|---|---|
| `FIT_TOL` 0.01 -> 0.1 | 4 |
| `STRAIGHT_TOL` 0.01 -> 0.1 | 1 |
| `from_face` no-area guard dropped | 1 |
| `fit` no-width guard dropped | 1 |
| `from_edges` zero-length guard dropped | 1 |
| `confine` finite / width > 0 guard -> `if false` | 1 |
| `judge` -> plain confine error | 1 |
| inscribe off (`fit.width -= 2.0 * out` dropped) | 2 |
| `INSCRIBE_MAX` 0.05 -> 0.2 or 1.0 | 1 |
| face wall law dropped | 6 |
| face end law dropped | 1 |
| `slot_bound_of`: 3+ edges use the first two / face+edges uses the face / patch-vertex `continue` / gone model `continue` | 1 each |
| `CreateOperation` seed dropped | 1 |
| **`seg_seg_dist`: crossing branch dropped (`return 0.0` removed)** | **0 - all pins pass** |

### Requested before merge
1. **Pin the crossing branch of `seg_seg_dist`** (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_face.rs:31-34`). Without it, a boundary segment that crosses the slot's centre line, with both endpoints more than `r` away, is measured by its endpoint distances only. That is exactly the thin wall the sampling used to miss. With the branch removed, the slit-hole face above is accepted silently (`confine` returns `Ok`), and no pin goes red. In every current pin the wall segment's endpoint lies within `r` of the centre segment, so the endpoint distances alone catch it. Fix: add a pin like the following to `slot_room_pins.rs` (I checked locally that it goes red with the branch removed and green with it in place):
   ```rust
   #[test]
   fn the_face_wall_law_refuses_a_thin_wall_across_the_slot() {
       // A 0.1 mm slit hole across the slot; all its vertices outside the
       // slot's outline - only the segment crossing test sees it.
       let reg = Region::new(vec![
           Loop::new(vec![p(10.0, -5.0), p(20.0, -5.0), p(20.0, 25.0), p(10.0, 25.0)]).expect("outer"),
           Loop::new(vec![p(10.5, 10.22), p(10.5, 10.32), p(19.5, 10.32), p(19.5, 10.22)]).expect("slit"),
       ]).expect("region");
       let e = refused(&SlotBound::from_face(reg).expect("bound"), p(15.0, 0.0), p(15.0, 20.0), 6.0);
       assert!(e.contains("runs 3.000 mm outside the picked face"), "{e}");
   }
   ```

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **The cap is described loosely.** The `INSCRIBE_MAX` doc comment (`slot_room.rs:28-33`) and the decision file both say "the shrink is capped at 5% of the room's width". The code caps the radius draw-in per side (`out > INSCRIBE_MAX * w`), so the width can lose up to 10%. The 2-chords-per-quarter stadium above loses 7.6% (16.000 -> 14.782). That is still safe, since the slot ends up inside the face and the seeded width is shown, but the text should say "per side" or compare `2 * out`.
- **The second inscribe pass never changes anything.** After one pass the wall law reads <= 0. An end centre outside the face means `out > r`, which is always over the cap. The `0..2` loop is harmless, just redundant.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 8f6e00b3fa30bab79ffd9ce7d97a56b43f903d20 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (delta review b1e25d27..8f6e00b3, safety tier)

Scope: the one new commit `8f6e00b3` (no merge-of-main content in the delta).

### What looks good
- New pin `the_face_wall_law_refuses_a_thin_wall_across_the_slot` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_pins.rs:168`) covers the crossing branch of `seg_seg_dist`: a 0.1 mm slit whose vertices all sit farther than r from the centre line, so only the segment-crossing test can see it.
- `INSCRIBE_MAX` doc (`slot_room.rs:28`) and `docs/decisions/1504-slot-selection.md` now say "per side, width loses up to 10%", which matches the code (`slot_room.rs:232-235`: refuses `out > INSCRIBE_MAX * w`, then `fit.width -= 2.0 * out`).

### Local results (trial-merged with current main, clean)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Mutation: `return 0.0` in `seg_seg_dist` (`slot_room_face.rs:33`) removed | only the new pin goes red (15 passed, 1 failed) |
| Restored, motion lib `slot_room` | 16 passed |
| app `slot_picks` | 3 passed |
| app `slot_pick_refusals` | 7 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None. The blocker from the previous review is addressed.

### Notes (not blocking)
- The draw-in loop runs up to two passes (`for _ in 0..2`), each capped at 5% of `w` per side, so in principle the total draw-in could exceed the documented 10% of width on a second pass. In practice the second pass measures a residual overshoot that is far smaller; if you want the doc to be exact, cap the cumulative draw-in or say "per pass".
- SKULL's #1537 is stacked on this branch and needs a merge of the new head (8f6e00b3) before its own re-check.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
